Forecast Discussion

High pressure centered over the Mid-Atlantic coast kept a shallow wedge of cool, damp air over the mountains this morning. The last light showers were gone by midmorning. The wedge erodes, and the clouds break this afternoon.

The high slides offshore Tuesday, and a southwest wind returns. Tuesday is mild. Clouds increase Tuesday night, and some drizzle may return near the Blue Ridge.

Wednesday, a low tracks through the Great Lakes with an associated front approaching us from the west. Moisture rides north over the mountain region Wednesday. Light rain is possible in the morning, then rain develops from the south by late in the afternoon. Rain continues Wednesday night.

The cold front crosses the mountains early Thursday. Rain tapers off quickly Thursday morning, and the afternoon turns warmer with a few breaks in the clouds. Air behind this front is not much cooler.

A secondary front arrives Friday from the northwest with a noticeable northwest wind and cooler air. A few light showers may develop early Friday morning in the northwest flow along the west side of the Appalachians. Friday and Saturday are cooler and breezy under high pressure building from the Plains.

A reinforcing shot of cooler air approaches Sunday, with showers possible in the afternoon and at night.
